articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Fixes My Biggest Annoyance With Boss Fights
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero doesn’t make boss fights annoying, and I hope other devs pay attention.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Travis Northup. He loves action RPGs, including Phantom Blade Zero. Read his review here .

I play an obscene amount of soulslikes and sweaty action games, and although I largely enjoy my time facing off against these intentionally challenging gauntlets, one thing I’ve grown increasingly irritated by in recent years is something I’ve taken to calling the Scrub Tax .

But what is the Scrub Tax exactly? Well, it can take many forms. Sometimes it’s a nearly minute-long walk back to the lair of the boss I’m trying to beat. Or maybe it’s a super obnoxious unskippable cutscene I’m forced to watch every time you beat the boss’ first phase as they transform into an even more gruesome monster. Other times, it’s just a good ol’-fashioned 30-second loading screen that has me rubbing my temples in annoyance between failed runs. In other words, the Scrub Tax is an irritating procedure (intentional or otherwise) that games make you go through after getting yourself killed like the low-skill scrub that you are – things that waste your time unnecessarily beyond the hours you’re already investing in learning the encounter and “gitting gud.”

Phantom Blade Zero, though, shows us it doesn’t need to be this way, just by sprinkling a little sugar over the medicine that so many modern boss battles force you to swallow — Mary Poppins would be so proud.

Don’t get me wrong: I love getting my butt kicked in every single FromSoftware game – learning the attacks of some horrifying new foe and slowly building confidence after multiple deaths before utterly dominating the enemy is an impressively compelling loop. But I’m much less enthusiastic about the tiresome ways in which my time is wasted while I’m working to hone my skills. It’s already an odd choice to make players go through this kind of stuff in an era when more things are competing for our attention than ever before, but it’s an especially bizarre thing to include when you’ve specifically designed a game with repeated failure in mind .

This brings me to one of the most infuriating forms the Scrub Tax takes: a complete lack of checkpoints during boss fights. Nowadays it’s not just common, but almost universally accepted that if I die at any point in any phase of a boss fight, I should have to start over again from the very beginning. This means that every player is destined to spend significantly more time replaying through less exciting phases of these encounters than the later phases that are actually still challenging them. I can’t even count the number of times I’ve been excited for a final confrontation with a boss I’ve crawled over hot coals to face, only to find myself irritated 20 minutes later when I’m grinding through the first phase of the encounter for the 10th time, just so I can enjoy about 30 seconds of the second phase I keep dying on.

For example, I have a vivid memory of playing Lies of P for the first time and facing off against an extremely cool and challenging boss that had a very slow first phase. What should have been a highlight instead became incredibly frustrating. I’d fought my way through that first phase dozens of times, to the point where I’d done several completions of it in a row where I didn’t even take damage, effectively shifting gear into autopilot for the three minutes it took to get through it. By the time I finally did beat the final phase of this boss, I was so vexed at having over half of my time wasted repeating the first one that I couldn’t even enjoy my hard-fought victory.

This practice has become so shockingly common that I don’t even think most people understand just how much of their time is being wasted by these tedious roadblocks. In fact, this philosophy of game design has been so ingrained into my expectations that until I recently played through Phantom Blade Zero, it didn’t even occur to me just how much of a thorn in my side this has become. I can count on one hand the number of games that haven’t followed this format over the past decade, the most notable being Final Fantasy XVI, which isn’t really all that concerned with providing the player a challenge. God of War Ragnarok included the choice to turn on checkpoints for certain boss fights as an accessibility setting, which is an interesting option for those not wishing to bang their head up against a wall repeatedly, but I’m referring to a more specific niche of players who crave a tough fight and simply don’t want their time wasted. For people like me, having precious hours eaten up by tedious boss checkpoint design has simply become an accepted cost of doing business for a long time now.

Phantom Blade Zero has shattered the idea that this is just the way it has to be. Developer S-Game’s stellar action RPG succeeds not just because it’s full of badass, challenging boss fights that show off its grade-A combat, but because failure doesn’t cost you momentum. It trims a ton of fat and empty calories by making it easy to get right back into its showpiece showdowns. This improves its overall pacing massively. Instead of spending twice as long as you should on each boss fight, you work through each one at an incredibly steady clip, move on to the next obstacle faster, and, frankly, have more fun in the process. The 50 hours it took me to get through my first playthrough was such a refreshing experience; it made me increasingly irate that more games don’t choose to handle boss encounters this way.

“But Travis, adding checkpoints to boss fights trivializes difficulty, and we like difficulty.”

I agree that difficulty is a good thing! But if the only way you’re able to make your encounter difficult is by bloating its duration with multiple phases, effectively turning it into a test of patience as much as skill, then you have not created a very engaging boss battle. This kind of difficulty is aggravating because it’s so patently artificial . Most of the time I’m not being challenged at all by an opening phase that I’ve more or less committed to memory after a few runs – the challenge is in having the stamina to engage in the Sisyphean task of replaying the same series of blocks, parries, and dodges ad nauseam.

Wouldn’t it be nice if, by removing the need to replay prior phases, developers really took the gloves off and made those later rounds as brutal as their wicked hearts desired? Imagine a boss fight where half the attacks kill you instantly, and you don’t even mind because you’re only losing a handful of seconds with every failed run. I want to live in a world where instead of being punished as I go through the completely normal process of learning an encounter, every failure has almost zero friction to it.

Phantom Blade Zero - Donnie Yen Behind the Scenes Photos

Phantom Blade Zero is a fantastic reference point for this, because even when some of my deaths felt cheap (like attacks that killed me in one hit), it was incredibly easy to shrug off since I was instantly thrown right back into the action. PBZ’s philosophy of checkpointing bosses meant that I was less irritated by enemies who had ludicrously powerful attacks. That allows S-Game to experiment more with boss scenarios that simply would not fly in a game without checkpoints where the developers know each death is going to cost upwards of five minutes of your time. A death in Phantom Blade Zero is likely to cost you less than 30 seconds, so when the crazy badass warrior with a lightning spear impaled me on his weapon and launched me into space, I relished the loss and jumped right back into the fight. I want developers to be able to take more chances with boss encounters, and checkpointing is a truly powerful tool that allows them to do just that. By freeing us from repetition, it also unshackles the developer’s creativity.

Even if you think restarting from the beginning is something devs should keep around, surely there are better ways to handle this unnecessary Scrub Tax, right? For example, shouldn’t I be able to skip the first phase of a boss fight after I’ve managed to clear it without taking any damage? Or maybe after the tenth time I’ve beaten it consecutively, I finally get that checkpoint unlocked? Heck, feel free to take half of my healing items away if you want! I’m just trying to reclaim some of the lost time here – I don’t even mind if you want to make it harder.

I’m not saying that every developer should add checkpoints to boss fights immediately across the board, but Phantom Blade Zero has made me question whether or not it’s a good thing that so many games seem to forgo them by default. Elden Ring had the courtesy to drastically reduce the length of its runbacks to bosses when compared to earlier FromSoftware RPGs, but no checkpointing still meant a lot of time was spent repeating boss phases. Would defeating Malenia still have been satisfying had I been able to face off against her second, devilishly difficult form straight away after reaching it once? I think so.

I’ve come to the conclusion that forcing players to restart boss fights from scratch is quite a cheap way to make those encounters feel more challenging than they actually are, and I think that once players start finishing Phantom Blade Zero later this week, they might very well share the same revelation. In the meantime, I will continue my solitary war on the Scrub Tax, blade in hand, and ready for the next brutal boss.

Travis Northup is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter @TieGuyTravis and read his games coverage here .

articles.title: Scammers Are Taking Advantage of Hype for PS5 Emulators by Tricking Gamers Into Downloading Malware
articles.summary: Security experts have issued a warning over fake PS5 emulators after they found scammers were tricking gamers into downloading malware.
articles.body:
Security experts have issued a warning over fake PS5 emulators after they found scammers were tricking gamers into downloading malware.

NordVPN's Threat Intelligence research team said it had identified a scam campaign that was spreading malware through GitHub repositories disguised as PS5 emulation software for PC.

The scammers are exploiting two well-known emulator projects to trick gamers into downloading what appears to be an infostealer. The malware uses heavy anti-analysis tricks to evade detection, adds itself to Windows Defender exclusions, and deletes its own traces after infection, NordVPN said.

The scam campaign is taking advantage of increasing interest in PS5 emulation on PC, which has exploded in recent months as hackers use AI to assist their efforts. PS5 exclusives such as Astro Bot and the Demon’s Souls Remake, for example, were recently shown running on PC.

"Emulation fans are a perfect target. They are used to downloading experimental software from GitHub and running unsigned files, so nothing about this feels suspicious," said Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN. "But this is not an emulator. It steals your data, hides from your antivirus, and erases its own tracks before you notice anything is wrong."

Last week, Sony issued a new PS5 firmware update that some believe was designed to combat the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console . There is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security.

This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, which comes out next month, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

IGN reported on a hacker who had sparked an uproar within the PS5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.

articles.title: 'High-Tech' Atari Hotel With Esports Venue and Creator Studios Breaks Ground in Phoenix
articles.summary: Atari Hotels has officially broken ground in Phoenix, Arizona, with construction planned to complete in late 2028 to early 2029 for what could be the US’s next premier esports venue.
articles.body:
Atari Hotels has officially broken ground in Phoenix, Arizona, with construction planned to complete in late 2028 to early 2029 for what could be the US’s next premier esports venue.

First announced all the way back in January 2020, Atari Hotels promises to bring a combination of cutting-edge technology, first-of-its-kind entertainment, and hospitality to guests in the United States, with its first project now underway.

As told in a press release shared with IGN, groundbreaking will commence this week in Phoenix’s Roosevelt Row. The hotel is expected to feature “high-tech guest rooms,” creator studios, and an esports and concert venue that can house more than two thousand attendees, along with a sportsbook, “layers of immersive bars,” shopping, “immersive experiences,” and restaurants.

Currently, construction is in Phase One, which will demo the building currently on the property and begin work to lay the new hotel’s foundation. Phase Two will begin shortly after this is done. (Among its partners and celebrity investors is, oddly, FaZe Adapt, as well as American professional wrestler Henry Cejudo.)

“We’re pressing ‘start’ on Atari Hotels’ Phoenix property, bringing our vision for the first-of-its-kind venue closer to reality,” Jordan Taylor, a Partner at Intersection Development, said in a statement. “The opportunity to build an interactive venue like this in our hometown with an incredible partner like Atari is a privilege, and we’re excited to celebrate this milestone with the community as we break ground.”

“We’re excited to see construction begin on the Atari Hotel and believe in Intersection Development’s vision to create something that speaks to gaming as a consistent pillar of pop culture,” Wade Rosen, Chairman and CEO of Atari, added. “This project puts the Atari brand at the heart of a brand-new entertainment experience for fans, tourists, and Phoenix locals.”

The Atari Hotel is being designed by räkkhaus, which describes itself as an “an avant-garde architecture studio that embodies the fusion of love, form, and revolution.” Given that it's licensed by Atari, the hotel will combine gaming and hospitality with hopes to “capitalize on the growing intersection of gaming, sports, entertainment, and pop culture.”

The first concept art for the property made its way online in October 2020, showing a Cyberpunk exterior that looked like something straight out of Night City. This planned version of the hotel was shaped like the Atari logo, with the artwork showing off futuristic statues of robots and bright neon lighting. Newer images paint a different picture, though, and one that looks more appropriate for this time period.

This is almost as neat as the two Dragon Ball theme parks that are planned to be built in France and Qiddiya City. Concept art for the first park, shared in 2024, shows a giant Shenron statue on an island in the middle of a massive pond, with other areas seemingly taken straight out of the show.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Bloodborne Movie Gets Promising Update from Producer Jacksepticeye
articles.summary: Seán "Jacksepticeye" McLoughlin has provided an exclusive and promising update on the Bloodborne film to IGN.
articles.body:
Seán "Jacksepticeye" McLoughlin has provided an exclusive and promising update on the Bloodborne film to IGN.

While speaking with IGN about becoming the new elusive target in Hitman (out today), we naturally had to ask McLoughlin for an update on the Bloodborne movie, which he is producing . I pointed out that it's been over six months since the animated film was first announced , and at that time, it didn't have a writer or a director attached. McLoughlin confirmed to IGN that the film now has a writer and a director, and the movie is making great progress.

"Things are obviously much more along the pipeline than they were back then," he said. "It's one of those things that I personally would love to just say everything as a fan of this thing, but then there's no expectation, or there's no fun in the process. So we definitely have a lot more stuff mapped out where we're going with the story, and there are people in place to make this thing happen. Hopefully sooner than later, we can have announcements where we talk about who's involved and where it's going, and little teases of the story and where we're at with that.

"But I am proud of the work I've been doing on it. I think it's such an interesting job to have, and for me, it's fun to do. It can be really stressful as well at the same time because you're taking on such a monumental IP. And I am just there to be like, 'Hey, we need this pinprick perfect.' Will we ever get something perfect? I don't know. It's probably impossible to get everyone's expectations into one central pillar, but as someone who's brought on to do this job, I'm right in the position where I need to be, and we're poised to have something really cool."

As of right now, the team behind the film is keeping a lid on who the writer and director are. It's unclear when we'll learn more, but there are ample opportunities for reveals on the horizon - perhaps at The Game Awards this December, or during another gaming event next year. Speaking more about how the team is trying to translate Bloodborne to a new medium, McLoughlin noted that there's a big difference in how Bloodborne is an animated movie and Alex Garland's Elden Ring will be live action .

"We all have pie-in-the-sky dreams of doing that and making a huge story. And I guess we'll see what happens with Elden Ring, but even I don't think they're doing [the entirety of] Elden Ring. I'm sure they pick one part of that to be able to do because I mean, it'll cost you $600 million to do Elden Ring in live action.

"It's just the amount of time, effort, pieces moving, the amount of financials needed in place; is it even a smart decision to do it live action at that point, when there's a lot of stuff that you'd be able to do in animation that you can't do in live action, or you wouldn't nail down? And I think Bloodborne specifically is poised to do that well, because there's so much otherworldly aspects in that that would just be so cool to be able to blow the doors off animated rather than being like, 'Okay, put you in front of a green screen, and let's hope for the best.' Now, we can really whittle it down into something cool."

On the subject of the Elden Ring film, I also asked if his team has a plan to take any lessons from that project and apply it to the Bloodborne movie, or if there's such a difference in how they're making their respective movies that it won't be applicable.

"I mean, probably a bit of both. It is sort of a thing that it'll come out before ours. So you look at it and go, 'Okay, well, what did they do? What was their idea? Are we doing the similar things?' But I mean, Bloodborne and Elden Ring are so far apart from each other. The structure maybe is similar, but in terms of story [one is] Victorian England [and the other is] gods and a mountain [which are] very different from each other. So I would like to not take influence too much because you don't want to repeat the same things. And if it comes out, people are going to be upset, happy, indifferent. It's going to be a huge wide gamut of what people enjoy about different things. So hopefully give something people they don't expect, give them something that's interesting. And at the end of the day, it's all 'Why are we adapting it?'

"I don't want to adapt something if we're just going to tell the same stories with the same characters over and over and over again. Movies are a completely different medium than video games. What do movies do better than a game does? It's passive versus interactive, so how do we push and pull with that and play with different ideas? I think I don't want to be involved in an adaptation if it doesn't feel like there's a story worth telling within it or if it's not a good idea."

He went on to note that this isn't the first time he's taken a crack at a video game adaptation, as he'd previously tried to bring Soma to life, as well. Across all of these experiences, he hasn't had any interest in simply redoing the game in a new medium, but instead wants to find new stories that can expand universes, not unlike the Fallout series or the recent Resident Evil film .

"Whenever there's leeway in the story and there's latitude to tell different tales within universes, I think that's always most interesting. I don't really ever want to take an IP and just redo the game story. I think we've seen that happen so many times. I'm not going to name names of things, but people already have adaptations in their brains, but it just never really works out. Something like Fallout or Resident Evil are really good examples recently of for all intents and purposes, this is that world.

"We're just shifting the lens a little bit and we get something really interesting within that space. So I think those stories are worth telling because I remember we were at the BAFTA games and Ben Starr did an interview with somebody and he was talking about adaptation, how they shouldn't exist. And then everyone was tweeting at me being like, 'Do you and Ben hate each other now?' And I texted him being like, 'Dude, we're mortal enemies.' But he has the right idea that why are we adapting it is always the number one question."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Afterlife With Archie Lives Again in New Mausoleum Edition Hardcover
articles.summary: One of the best modern Archie stories ever published is rising from the grave, as Oni Press reveals the Afterlife With Archie: Mausoleum Edition hardcover.
articles.body:
Afterlife With Archie is undoubtedly one of the most successful revamps of the decades-old Archie franchise. Who doesn't love seeing this wholesome teen thrust into a world of zombies and brooding horror? Even as Oni Press kicks off a new era for the franchise, they're also celebrating this particular classic by teasing a new "Afterlife With Archie: Mausoleum Edition" hardcover set.

With the Kickstarter campaign for Afterlife With Archie: Mausoleum Edition Vol. 1 now live, IGN can exclusively reveal some of the artwork featured in this set. Check out the slideshow gallery below to see the exclusive posters and glow-in-the-dark cover art:

Afterlife With Archie: Mausoleum Edition Vol. 1 Preview Gallery

Afterlife With Archie was written by Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and illustrated by Francesco Francavilla. The series originally debuted in 2013 to rave reviews ( including on IGN ). Here's the official description of the new hardcover:

In the days before Halloween 2013, Archie Andrews, Jughead Jones, Betty Cooper, Veronica Lodge, and the rest of Riverdale’s beloved icons found themselves utterly transformed and powerfully reimagined as the comic industry’s most unlikely and unexpected horror anti-heroes within the pages of Harvey Award-winning writer Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Eisner Award-winning artist Francesco Francavilla’s AFTERLIFE WITH ARCHIE – detonating the first blast of a sold-out, smash-hit series that would immediately and definitively redefine the art and intensity of Archie Comics for a new generation. Unrelentingly celebrated by critics and ferociously followed by fans, AFTERLIFE WITH ARCHIE immediately became a jugular-ripping legend in its own time – due in no small part to the terrifying, tense, and uncannily atmospheric artwork of illustrator Francesco Francavilla, who quickly defined himself as one of his generation’s most instantly iconic and sought-after artists over the course of the series’ gut-wrenching run.

Now, on the cusp of the of the upcoming AFTERLIFE WITH ARCHIE live-action streaming series adaptation slated to debut on Disney+ in 2027, Oni Press and Archie Comics are pulling back the curtain to reveal Francavilla’s complete interior artwork and covers from AFTERLIFE WITH ARCHIE #1-6 in crisp and creepy B&W at the size of full-scale comics artboard and remastered by the artist himself.

The Kickstarter campaign for Afterlife With Archie: Mausoleum Edition Vol. 1 features plenty of optional bonuses, including signed copies from Aguirre-Sacasa and Farncavilla, the aforementioned posters, T-shirts, enamel pins, and reprints of the individual issues.

For more, check out IGN's reviews of all three of Oni Press' rebooted Archie comics .

articles.title: FromSoftware's Nintendo Switch 2 Exclusive The Duskbloods Officially Delayed Into 2027
articles.summary: FromSoftware has announced a delay of The Duskbloods to 2027. The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive was due out by the end of 2026.
articles.body:
FromSoftware has announced a delay of The Duskbloods to 2027. The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive was due out by the end of 2026.

In a statement published online, the Dark Souls and Elden Ring developer said that it had decided to delay the game following feedback from the recent network test, with a focus on combat, strategic depth, and player expression.

There’s no word on when in 2027 The Duskbloods will launch.

Fans had braced themselves for a delay after The Duskblood was among a number of no-shows at the September 2026 Nintendo Direct . Before that, in August, FromSoftware brought The Duskbloods network test to an early end after the first day of testing resulted in "game server issues" that barred players from logging in.

FromSoftware is responsible for some of the most influential games of the last 20 years, including 2022 masterpiece Elden Ring. So anticipation for The Duskbloods to recreate some of that FromSoftware magic on Switch 2 is sky high.

articles.title: Some People Who Paid for WoW Forever Name Reservation Couldn't Reserve Their Name Due to a Weird Bug
articles.summary: After the World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, Blizzard opened up the servers to character creation in order to allow players who bought one of the Skyborne packs to reserve their names. But a lot of people were falsely given a "restricted" message when they tried to reserve their name.
articles.body:
After the World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, Blizzard opened up the servers to character creation in order to allow players who bought one of the Skyborne packs to reserve their names. But a lot of people were falsely given a "restricted" message when they tried to reserve their name.

Even after the rough start that Blizzard's name reservation system had on Tuesday , some players weren't able to reserve their name, with the character creation screen telling them their name was on the restricted list. Blizzard has since fixed the problem, and told players it was due to a bugged name filter.

Community manager Kaivax took to the WoW Forever forums to explain: "In WoW Forever, we’ve been working on the restricted name list, which is a list the game uses to check for non-profane names that we wish to restrict, such as major Warcraft lore characters or names that are blocked for technical reasons. Today we’ve determined that we have a bug in the process that caused the game to be overly restrictive with some names. For example, it has been incorrectly restricting names containing 'c-o-n.'"

In the replies to Kaivax's post, it was made clear that the name filter was a bit overzealous. Player Nursejoy posted: "Major Warcraft lore characters? I understand that but it seems any named NPC is on the list. Example: Generically named NPCs 'Nurse' and 'Officer' hardly hold major Warcraft lore but names containing 'nurse' are restricted. This is a specifically bad example to illustrate impact." They then went on to list 23 different character names with the word 'nurse' that they supposedly tried to reserve, but couldn't.

According to Kaivax, the fixes should have gone live with the server restart, but some players are still reporting problems reserving their names. However, I've been able to go in and reserve the name 'Concon Concon,' so the specific combination that Kaivax mentioned does seem to have been fixed at least.

But while this overly strict name filter appears to have been a bug, WoW Forever has been fairly strict on character names. There was a controversy relatively early in the beta about names being reported, and Blizzard had to come out and reassure players that humans were reviewing the reports . I also got a chance to sit down with WoW Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut to talk about the future of the game , and it seems like the team is laser-focused on making it an even more social version of the MMO.

articles.title: Dune: Part 3 Has 3 Popcorn Buckets, Including One With 2 Sandworm Mouths
articles.summary: With Dune: Part 3 fast approaching, AMC Theatres has finally shown off the movie's popcorn buckets. Fittingly, there are three.
articles.body:
With Dune: Part 3 fast approaching, AMC Theatres has finally shown off the movie's popcorn buckets. Fittingly, there are three.

There’s one with two sandworm mouths, so you can share popcorn with other Dune-heads. Another features one mouth hole and a thumper that actually moves up and down while you munch your snacks.

The final popcorn-themed concession collectible is a bucket shaped like the mobile containment tank of the Guild Navigator, Edric, who we’ll likely get to know better in Dune: Part 3. The collectibles were officially revealed on the AMC Theatres Instagram page .

Dune: Part 3 is based on Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah, and takes place 17 years after the events of the first two films. Timothée Chalamet returns as Paul Atreides, who you know has probably gone too far this time because he’s shaved his head. Bald dudes mean business.

Meanwhile, Zendaya has an expanded role as Chaya and will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category at the Oscars. Both previous Dune movies were nominated in technical excellence categories, but the actors didn’t get any nods.

Even if you think you know the book it’s based on, however, we might be in for some big surprises. The final trailer for Dune: Part 3 suggested some major deviations from the source material.

Dune: Part 2 surpassed the previous movie in the trilogy at the box office , generating almost $500 million. Dune: Part 1 grossed $433 million worldwide during its entire theatrical run. However, the first movie was released simultaneously in theaters and on HBO Max, giving people the option of watching it at home with their own popcorn buckets.

Dune: Part 3 is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 18, 2026, with early IMAX preview screenings beginning on December 14, 2026.

articles.title: Minecraft Creator Notch Is Selling His L.A. Mansion for the 'Low' Asking Price of $70 Million
articles.summary: Markus “Notch” Persson sold Minecraft developer Mojang to Microsoft back in 2014 for a cool $2.5 billion, then moved to the U.S. and casually outbid Jay-Z and Beyonce for a Beverly Hills mansion. At the time, it cost him $70 million. Now, he's selling up.
articles.body:
Markus “Notch” Persson sold Minecraft developer Mojang to Microsoft back in 2014 for a cool $2.5 billion, then moved to the U.S. and casually outbid Jay-Z and Beyonce for a Beverly Hills mansion . At the time, it cost him $70 million. Now, he's selling up.

Despite L.A.’s median home value more than doubling, Notch is looking for a quick sale on the mansion, a 22,300-square-foot estate which features 15 bathrooms, a $200,000 candy room, and its own private nightclub.

According to the L.A. Times , the market for housing for the super rich has cooled in the past decade, hence the “low” asking price.

If it sells, it’ll be the most expensive home sale in Beverly Hills this year and the second-priciest in L.A. County. When Notch bought it, the house boasted a 2,500-bottle wine cellar, and an art installation with a chrome machine gun as the centrepiece, as well as eight bedrooms, 15 bathrooms, a movie theatre and a swimming pool.

Notch added the nightclub, as well as a recording studio and a DJ booth to host parties for the rich and famous of Beverly Hills. According to Notch, he doesn’t spend much time in L.A. anymore, hence the sale.

Interestingly, he’s not alone. The listing coincided with a broader L.A. exit by tech moguls. Mark Zuckerberg and Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin have set up homes in Florida to avoid Proposition 40, a proposed wealth tax being voted on next week which would, if passed, levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.

Apparently, it’s a cause that’s united the rich. According to Politico , a record $612 million from more than 70 current and former California billionaires was pumped into this year’s state elections, with almost 50% of the funds aimed at defeating Proposition 40. Notch didn’t mention the tax as a reason for listing the property.

The Minecraft creator hasn’t put out any major video games since he sold Minecraft to Microsoft. The game is still one of the most popular in the world and continues to get regular updates. Microsoft recently launched Minecraft Dungeons 2 , a sequel spinoff that turns the blocky Minecraft characters into warriors and mages in a Diablo-esque dungeon crawler. A Minecraft Movie, the big screen adaptation of the game, blew past $700 million at the box office. A sequel is in the works.

articles.title: The Hellraiser Franchise Is Getting Three New Tabletop Adaptations for Halloween 2027
articles.body:
Pinhead and the rest of the Hellraiser crew are seeing quite the resurgence right now, and that looks to continue into next year. Announced today, Salt Entertainment has revealed that they have entered an agreement with Clive Barker and Park Ave Ent. LLC to release not one, not two, but three official Hellraiser tabletop games with the first of these planned for release Halloween 2027. Perfectly timed to coincide with the 40th anniversary of the original film .

Salt’s currently slated hellish titles begin with Hellraiser: Puzzle of Flesh from designer Travis Chance (Cthulul: Dark Providence, Heroes Wanted) a dice-based / push-your-luck title themed around the franchise's signature Lament Configuration box. Coming in a custom box modeled after the artifact (which doubles as the game’s dice tumbler) Salt describes it as an “escape-room style and social deduction game in which hidden desires, shifting loyalties and questionable choices make it increasingly difficult to know whom - or what - to trust”. These devilish little boxes are some of the most recognizable relics from the films and I will be excited to see how what they represent gets adapted for the ol’ weekly game night when it releases next Halloween.

If you would prefer something more story driven, then you are in luck too as a fullblown Hellraiser tabletop RPG is also in the works. This project is being helmed by designer Franceso Nepitello who has a little experience in adapting big properties into TTRPGs, being the co-designer of The One Ring RPG based on the Lord of the Rings. Others may know him for another little game set in that universe, War of the Ring - a game we consider one of the best LoTR board games period . This RPG looks to allow fans to expand and open up the Hellraiser universe to let you explore and play out your own stories of temptation, desire, and the horrors that lie beyond our own world.

“I wanted to design a horror roleplaying game for years,” said Nepitello. “Getting to do it with Hellraiser is incredibly exciting. Its blend of dread, desire and forbidden knowledge offers so much to explore at the gaming table. I can’t wait to open the box with the players.”

Last up for this initial slate of games is the one I am most excited to learn more about. Headed up by game designer Michael Shinall, the guy behind other games such as Marvel Zombies, a Song of Ice & Fire: Tabletop Miniatures Game, Bloodborne: The Board Game , and most recently the Tasting History board game also being produced by Salt Entertainment (and currently on Kickstarter ). Out of the three this is the one we know the least about, only being described as “a major new Hellraiser board game”, On the topic of working with such a legendary property, Shinall has a solid grasp on what this IP means, "Hellraiser is unique among the horror world as, outside brilliant monster and world design, it delves into the reaches of the human psyche in ways that many others have tried to emulate, but often failed to reach. It accepts that the truest horrors are never external, but the inner depths of the darkest parts of the soul... And I look forward to bringing that to a new medium."

Speaking with Geoff Skinner, President of Salt Entertainment regarding Barker’s input on these projects, he had this to say; “Yes, Clive Barker is approving everything and guiding our creative, so we are all on our A-game. We’re using not only the films as a basis, but also the original novella, Hellbound Heart. It’s always a treat to work with the original creator of any brand, but to be working with someone who shaped the culture so heavily is an absolute honor. More details involving Puzzle of Flesh, the TTRPG, and Shinalls major board game project will be revealed over the coming months with the titles planned for release for the retail market.

articles.title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
articles.summary: It’s also time to name the next Elder Scrolls game, and Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving.
articles.body: To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft’s workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India. It’s the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the retirement offer that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It’s all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft’s operating costs and headcount. “Our total people costs will go down, our cost per head will go up, and my GPU per researcher will go up,” Nadella said on a podcast almost two years ago, responding to a question about AI’s impact on headcount. That’s a financial way of saying Microsoft will have fewer people, but it will offer higher salaries and more tools and AI power to those who remain. It also helps explain the continued layoffs we’ve seen at Microsoft over the past couple of years. Microsoft has been performing layoffs regularly over the past decade, but over the past couple of years, the layoffs and executive departures have been significant. These aren’t the annual layoffs of old; they’re now happening every few months. This week’s voluntary exit offer arrived just months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 employees, cuts that impacted its Xbox and commercial sales teams the most. For the first time in a decade, Microsoft’s overall headcount has also gone down year over year. Microsoft now employs around 223,000 people as of June 30th, 5,000 fewer than the 228,000 people it employed in 2025. Microsoft laid off 4 percent of its workforce in July last year, and it’s now offering voluntary buyout offers to around a quarter of its employees. More than 30 percent of the 9,000 eligible employees accepted a retirement offer earlier this year, but that number will likely be far less for the company’s latest Voluntary Exit Offer. That’s largely because, according to sources familiar, the offer is practically the same as regular severance terms at Microsoft — cash based on time at the company, accelerated stock vesting, some additional subsidized health coverage, and several months of career services. But what makes this unusual is the scale of the amount of employees who have been offered this exit. Even if only 5 percent accept the offer, that’s still 3,000 employees. I understand eligible employees have until December to decide, so we won’t know the impact of this offer for a while yet. With rumors of more layoffs in November and January, the amount of employees who do accept will surely inform Microsoft’s numbers for its next round of cuts. There are some, both inside and outside the company, who think Microsoft needs these cuts. “Microsoft needs fewer people,” says Merill Fernando, a former Microsoft Entra product manager. “I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.” Fernando paints a picture of a Microsoft where every organization “had its own priorities and its own decision makers,” so it’s hard to get the company to do anything collectively. It sounds a little like the meme where each organization in Microsoft is pointing guns at each other, competing instead of collaborating. Nadella even addressed that meme last year in a podcast with Stripe co-founder John Collison, acknowledging that the comic has defined Microsoft’s cultural narrative “more so than reality,” but that it had signaled some very real tensions inside the company. “In some sense, some of these divisional tensions are real issues that need to have tension. Social cohesion is not a goal, winning in the marketplace is a goal,” said Nadella. The question now is whether Nadella can reshape Microsoft for the AI era without undoing the cultural transformation that helped define his leadership. A company that has shifted to be built around empathy is now asking its employees to reckon with an AI future that could make many of their jobs unnecessary. How Nadella handles that transition will define his legacy as much as the growth and success he’s achieved over the past decade. Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving after nearly 27 years A few weeks ago I started hearing from Xbox employees that Dan Greenawalt, the longtime creative force behind Forza Motorsport, is leaving after almost 27 years. Greenawalt is departing as the head of Turn 10 Studios, the Forza Motorsport creator that merged with Forza Horizon developer Playground Games. Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams revealed the news in a recent internal memo, seen by Notepad. “Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,” says Williams. Greenawalt will stay on as an adviser to Williams and the newly appointed Playground Games chief operating officer, Michel Bastien, “while he transitions to his next phase.” Here’s part of Williams’ memo about Greenawalt: > It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original XBOX in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next. Microsoft revealed last month that it was merging its two Forza developers into a single studio as part of a massive restructuring of Xbox. Both Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios have merged into just Playground Games. The studio now has two locations: Playground Games Leamington Spa and Playground Games Redmond. With Greenawalt retiring and Turn 10 merged into Playground Games, it’s not clear if we’ll ever see Microsoft return to Forza Motorsport. More than 70 people at Turn 10 Studios were laid off last year, in a move that hit the vast majority of the studio. Over the past year, Turn 10 Studios has essentially been maintaining Forza Motorsport, and now the remaining employees have moved to Playground Games to work on Forza Horizon and Fable. It’s time to name The Elders Scrolls VI: Sentinel It’s been more than eight years since Bethesda officially announced the existence of the sixth game in its Elder Scrolls series. While there have been some debates around platform exclusivity for The Elder Scrolls VI, we’ve heard very little detail about the game that Bethesda has been working on all this time. Sources familiar with Bethesda’s plans tell me that the Xbox-owned publisher is about to announce that the next Elder Scrolls game will officially be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. The announcement could come as soon as next month, during a period that will mark 15 years since The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim was released. Bethesda has been showing off Sentinel gameplay in recent months, I’m told. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma got a live playthrough of Sentinel in August, and she praised the scale of the game and said “the story is even greater.” While I’m only expecting a name reveal next month and nothing more, I’ve been hearing some additional details about the game. If you want to totally avoid spoilers about the game, then don’t read the next paragraph. I understand that Sentinel will be set in Hammerfell, a province in the Elder Scrolls universe that’s appeared in The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard and The Elder Scrolls Online. Sentinel will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls, and help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts. The pad * Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months. This is a weird one. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years. She previously served as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox COO in July. The sudden departure was announced in a surprisingly short memo from Xbox chief Asha Sharma last week. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” says Sharma. It doesn’t seem like the Xbox COO position is going away, as Sharma notes that “we’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.” Eurogamer reported over the weekend that Chiang had been “terminated for policy violations.” I’ve heard similar chatter internally, but Chiang has been described to me by multiple Xbox employees as highly respected, with high integrity, so this turn of events is quite odd. I’m trying to get more details, but if you’ve heard anything, please reach out confidentially at notepad@theverge.com or through the secure Signal messaging app. (I’m tomwarren.01.) * Microsoft’s new Surface Laptop Ultra update fixes reboot and display bugs. I ran into some weird issues with the Surface Laptop Ultra during my review, and Microsoft is now fixing some of them with a firmware update. The update addresses screen flickering, unexpected restarts, and lengthy reboot times alongside unspecified “additional bug fixes and general performance improvements.” I’m still waiting to see if Nvidia or Microsoft addresses the strange laggy feeling on the Surface Laptop Ultra, and it’s too early to say whether this firmware update addresses that or not yet. * GitHub’s former CEO launched a competing platform for AI agents. We knew that Thomas Dohmke, former GitHub CEO, was building some kind of competitor to GitHub, but the result has surprised people internally during the week of GitHub’s Universe conference. Developers can use the new Entire platform to host and review code, but it’s also designed to work with AI agents and replaces pull requests with a “Trails” feature that offers “customizable evals that are scored by agents on every code push.” One GitHub employee tells me, “people are shocked, they have ambushed us up and down the stack on our own conference week.” * Windows will soon let you perform an internet speed test without opening your browser. Microsoft added a speed test option to the Windows 11 taskbar earlier this year, but it was just a link to a speed test in Bing that opened in your browser. Now, Microsoft is actually integrating a full speed test into the taskbar, so you can right-click the network icon and perform an internet speed test right there. * Windows 11 is getting some neat trackpad features. Microsoft is adding new Windows trackpad features that let you scroll through long documents and webpages faster. You’ll also be able to continuously scroll through a page by swiping the edge of your touchpad, along with support for single-finger scrolling. It’s the small things that count, and I love to see these kinds of features being added to Windows. * Microsoft says its AI tool is better than doctors at diagnosing conditions. Microsoft claims to have developed an AI-powered tool that it says can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human doctors. The findings were published last week in Science, one of the world’s most prestigious journals. Microsoft has pitted its AI system against human physicians on a series of scenarios drawn from medical case reports and emergency department data. While there’s still a long road ahead before this AI system can be widely deployed, Microsoft thinks its work is significant. “It needs clinical validation,” says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman in an interview with The Verge. “That is a leap, but this is a major milestone along that journey.” * Microsoft Authenticator flaw lets malicious Android apps steal tokens. Security researchers at Enclave have discovered a vulnerability with Microsoft Authenticator that lets an unprivileged Android app with zero permissions “impersonate any installed Microsoft first-party app and have the Microsoft Authenticator broker hand it that app’s tokens.” The tokens could provide full access to mailboxes, files, and calendars. Microsoft has now fixed the flaw, and if you use Microsoft Authenticator on Android, then it’s time to update it immediately. * Denmark has abandoned plans to ditch Microsoft Office after technical problems. Last year the government of Denmark announced it was ditching Windows and Office in favor of open-source alternatives to reduce its reliance on US vendors. It seems like the trial of moving away from Microsoft’s software hasn’t gone too well for the Danish government, though. The Danish Ministry of Digitalisation has reportedly ended its trial for an open-source alternative to Microsoft Office. Employees reportedly encountered issues with document formatting, blank pages, and tracking changes. * Gears of War: E-Day cost $500 million to make. Gears of War E-Day has the highest Metacritic score of any entry in the franchise since the Xbox 360 days, but it faces some tough questions around how much it costs to create a AAA game these days and what success looks like. Kotaku reports that E-Day cost “over $500 million” to make, excluding marketing budgets. This has generated a lot of discussion online over E-Day’s success, especially as it’s a controversial test for any potential return to Xbox exclusivity. One source tells me that more than 400,000 copies of the game have been sold across Xbox and Steam, but the big question is whether Microsoft was happy with its Game Pass numbers for E-Day, and whether that revenue offsets any additional sales on Xbox and potential PS5 sales if a port had been released. * Arkane Lyon and Blade could be about to be saved. Earlier this year, I reported that Microsoft was weighing up canceling its Blade game and shuttering Arkane. In the months since June, Microsoft has been in ongoing discussions with multiple publishers about a potential sale of Arkane Lyon amid consultations with the union representing the studio’s employees. French newspaper Le Monde now reports that Microsoft has a November 13th cutoff date for a decision on the future of Arkane Lyon, and Microsoft confirmed to PC Gamer that it’s extending this deadline by an additional month. An extension makes it seem like Microsoft is close to a deal, and I’m cautiously optimistic that Blade will be saved. We’ll find out in the coming weeks. * Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs. After nearly two years of Copilot support on smart TVs, Microsoft is pulling the plug. I’d love to know how many people actually used Copilot this way, because it can’t be more than a dozen. LG says the Copilot TV feature is “scheduled for discontinuation during 2026” and a specific date is “subject to Microsoft’s timeline.” * Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul. Microsoft overhauled its financial reporting this quarter, placing Windows, Surface, and Xbox in a separate bucket to its more revenue generating AI and cloud efforts. Windows OEM revenue was down 22 percent amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market drop by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Xbox hardware and content and services were also down, but a whole third of Microsoft’s revenue came from Azure ($33.17 billion of the $92.3 billion). I thought Nadella’s most interesting remarks on the earnings call were about Microsoft’s own AI models. “Our goal is to advance the cost to outcome frontier, which means delivering capabilities comparable to leading models within three to six months of their release at a fraction of the training cost, thereby allowing us to transfer those cost benefits to customers,” said Nadella. I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there. Thanks for subscribing to Notepad.

articles.title: PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset Is Up for Preorder for $99, and It’s Out the Same Day as GTA 6
articles.summary: PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset preorders are live now. It's out November 19, the same day as GTA 6.
articles.body:
Heads up, PS5 owners: the PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset is now available for preorder. It comes in white or Midnight Black color schemes and is up at most of the usual retailers for $99. It's out November 19, which also happens to be the same day Grand Theft Auto VI releases. Coincidence? I honestly don’t know, but if you’re planning late-night GTA 6 sessions and don’t want to keep the roomies awake, having a brand-new pair of wireless headphones for your PS5 certainly won’t hurt.

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset - White

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset (White)

The white version has a white headband, while the Midnight Black version has a black one.

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset - Midnight Black

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset (Midnight Black)

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset is a wireless headset designed for PS5 (naturally), with both PlayStation Link connectivity as well as Bluetooth, so it’ll work with other devices as well. It also features simultaneous connectivity, which lets you swap between, for instance, your PS5 and your phone instantly.

Sony touts it as having Tempest 3D audio support, which offers immersive sound that seems to come from all around you. It has planar magnetic drivers, which are supposed to produce “lifelike sound.” The built-in microphones let you do things like use in-game chat or talk on your phone, and it has “AI-enhanced noise rejection,” for clearer communication no matter what noise is going on in the background.

You can turn the earcups to flatten the headset out, making it easier to pack in a bag to take on the go. Basically, it’s a new Sony headset that ought to work excellently and seamlessly on the PS5. And it comes out the same day as GTA 6, giving you a good opportunity to try it out.

This new headset effectively replaces the Pulse 3D Wireless headset that we gave a 9/10 in our review . Here's hoping this new model is even better. I certainly like the look of the new one over the old one.

It's also worth noting that Sony is going to release the higher-end PlayStation Pulse Edge Wireless Headset, which was announced at the same time as this one, at some point early next year. It will feature active noise cancellation, but will cost more. The exact price and release date have yet to be announced.

In related news, for those who prefer earbuds to headphones, you can save $50 on PlayStation Pulse Explore Wireless Earbuds right now at Amazon .

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Pokémon Happy Meals Are Coming Back to McDonald's — Here's What Cards and Toys Are Included This Year
articles.summary: Pokémon Happy Meals are coming back to McDonald's, and the fast-food giant has officially confirmed what toys and cards you can collect from this round of the promotion.
articles.body:
Pokémon Happy Meals are coming back to McDonald's, and after a series of leaks hit social media, the fast-food giant has officially confirmed which toys and cards you can collect from this round of the collaboration.

The Pokémon promotion launches November 10 in the U.S. and will expand to over 70 countries in the following months. The Happy Meal comes in three different boxes, each of which includes one of 15 Pokémon toys and two of 15 reprinted cards.

The specific list of cards Pokémon has revealed doesn’t exactly line up with what McDonald’s and leakers have been sharing online, possibly pointing to different offerings by region. The fast-food chain also hasn’t confirmed whether there will be any specific food or meal items — for now, it’s all about the collectibles.

The three Happy Meal boxes feature Pikachu, Torchic, and Umbreon. The toys are essentially mini versions of those boxes, displaying individual Pokémon's faces under the classic golden arches handle. While they may not be that fun to play with or big enough to use as an actual container, they at least require a little bit of effort to put together.

Here's the 15 pocket monsters that are getting the toy box treatment:

Like previous McDonald’s collaborations, the included cards are stamped reprints with McDonald’s numbering (M27, this time around), and seven are confetti holo.

A full announcement on the Pokémon site includes a list of 15 cards, shown above, though Pokémon’s list differs from cards that McDonald’s accounts (and leakers ) have been sharing on social media.

One McDonald’s announcement image has cards dedicated to Pikachu, Palafin, Mimikyu, Chandelure, Decidueye, Tyranitar. That list actually lines up with the cards leakers have been sharing online, which also include Zoroark, Wooloo, Snorlax, Eevee, Jirachi, Metagross, Absol, Hawlucha, and Lucario.

3 boxes. 15 toys. 2 cards with every collectible. Pokémon Happy Meal coming 11.10.26. — McDonald's (@McDonalds) October 29, 2026

3 boxes. 15 toys. 2 cards with every collectible. Pokémon Happy Meal coming 11.10.26.

McDonald's accounts also confirm the promotion will be coming to over 70 countries over the next couple of months, with progressive launches through February next year. Toys and cards will likely vary by region, which may be the cause of the card list confusion. For example, Quebec locations will not have the Happy Meal toys, instead offering a Pokémon sticker and a mini booster pack with four cards.

As for how much time Trainers will have to collect 'em all, Pokémon and McDonald’s are only going with “as long as supplies last.” X users, however, had been sharing images from their local McDonald’s store in the lead-up to the collaboration’s official announcement. One unconfirmed image shows the promotion running in U.S. locations from November 10 through December 14.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: All Memory Flower Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Memory Flowers are your only way of increasing your total health pool in Phantom Blade 0. Collecting sets of flowers will increase your health by different
articles.body:
Memory Flowers are your only way of increasing your total health pool in Phantom Blade 0. Collecting sets of flowers will increase your health by different percentages; some will be a 5% increase, while others may be 7%. You'll want to go out of your way to get every single one you can, so below you'll find the location of every Memory Flower in the game. You can click on a zone to go directly to it if you're just hunting for a few pesky ones you've missed.

As you progress the main story of Phantom Blade 0, you'll be introduced to Memory Flowers. Glowing blue flowers that sprout on the ground and offer a bit of insight into the memories of characters from the surrounding areas. The Crimson Forest has 16 Memory Flowers to find, many of which are found on the main path, and a handful tucked away in some clever ways.

You'll come across the first Memory Flower after the cutscene with Lady Inaris plays shortly after entering the Crimson Forest and interacting with the Crane Bell. Directly to the right of the bell, you'll see the first Memory Flower.

After you defeat Hua Qianxiao on the broken bridge, drop off the edge and turn around, use the Chain Sickle Phantom Edge to cross the gap. Follow the path, and you'll find the second Memory Flower surrounded by three enemy dogs you need to defeat before picking up the flower.

Upon talking to Quick Hand Zhang in the hanging Cage, you'll be asked to go into the cavern to free him. Once inside, you'll see the next Memory Flower on the ledge below surrounded by a few enemies. Dispatch the enemies to pick up Memory Flower 3.

At the Outlaw Trap Bell, head right and follow the dirt path. You'll need a mounted enemy and a thief guarding the flower. Defeat them and grab Memory Flower 4.

Once you've defeated Jing The Outlaw, go left. As you approach the wooden bridge look to your right, where you'll see a small ledge to drop down. This is where Memory Flower 5 is located.

As you cross the bridge, you'll enter a small village. Follow the path to the left and take the wooden path that bends around the mountain as you continue left. Inside the cavern, you'll find Memory Flower 6 right inside.

As you progress the main path and continue pushing forward, you'll come across a small residence on a cliffside.

Once inside the Crimson Forest Cellar. Found on the first floor of the seemingly abandoned house on the cliffside, drop all the way down between the two wooden scaffolds. The Memory Flower will be tucked between the chasm.

Continuing on the main path, you'll be ambushed by a large enemy known as the Smasher. After being chased by the Smasher, you'll find the Memory Flower directly in front of you at the Mirrorwood Entrance.

Upon defeating Iron Fever, the next Memory Flower will be found on the ridge just north of the arena.

Once you grab Memory Flower 9, immediately turn around to look where you dropped down into the arena from. You'll notice an uphill pathway just right of the entrance. Follow that path to find Memory Flower 10 at the top of this other path.

On the main path, you'll find the next Memory Flower right next to the Burial Grounds Bell. Clear the enemies in the area in order to pick it up.

Go past the Burial Ground Bell and follow the main path. You'll find Memory Flower 12 as soon as you enter the wooded area in the next section.

After obtaining Memory Flower 12, head north and drop down the ledge at the edge of this small area. You'll find Memory Flower 13 right there.

Across the riverbed, you'll see Memory Flower 14 tucked right by the entrance to the next section of the Mirrorowood Forest.

Crimson Forest Memory Flower 15 & Crimson Forest Memory Flower 16

As you progress through the portal puzzle here, the Memory Flowers will appear in the middle of the room.

Those are all of the Memory Flowers found in the Crimson Forest. This is just the beginning, though, as there are still plenty more to go in the upcoming zones. Snagging all of these now will give you a decent boost to your overall health and make the upcoming fights a bit easier to deal with.

As you travel around the Village of Lu you'll want to stop around and grab these Memory Flowers as you go by. These flowers are the only way to increase your overall health pool in Phantom Blade 0 so you don't want to miss them. Below you'll find all of the Memory Flowers for the Village of Lu map.

Found to the right of the Mandate Encampment Outer Gate Bell. You'll see it if you follow the path up to the Mandate Gate on the east side of the Village of Lu

Found immediately after defeating Zhou Bi, The Gatekeeper. To the left of the arena, you'll see the memory flower through the small gateway. Two children will be looking at the flower.

From the Covered Bridge Bell, go through the gateway to its right. Follow the path down and around through the building and the field with the scarecrow. You'll find the next Memory Flower at an altar with about 5 enemies praying to it. It will also be marked with a Purple Icon on your map for the Secrets at the Heart of the Lake quest

Upon crossing the Covered Bridge, follow the path until you can fork right. A large lady enemy will be blocking the doorway to a house. Defeat her and go down the ladder found inside the house. A hole in the wall will lead outside, where you'll find the next Memory Flower on the ridge.

Upon defeating Master Bi Yuan of the Tianxuan Sect, you'll find a newly sprouted Memory Flower in the arena

After picking up Memory Flower 5, turn around and head toward the small stairs leading up to the house across the way. Head inside and make a left. The next Memory Flower will be in the room.

After defeating Master Bi, Hai of Kuye Temple, you'll find the next Memory Flower in the middle of the battle arena

After grabbing Memory Flower 7 head upstream toward the purple glowing chest containing a Blackstone Fragment in it. Continue past the chest until you reach the end of the river, here you'll find a few enemies and another Memory Flower.

From the Terraces Bell head into the house on your right. Inside, you'll find Memory Flower 9 sitting on a table.

Upon reaching the Engine Giant Remains Bell, head inside the shrine and attack the human body that is impaling the spear into the giant monster. After the body is destroyed Memory Flower 10 will be in its place.

After grabbing Memory Flower 10 drop down the hole in front of you. Follow the dirt road path to the left hopping over the fallen tree. You'll see the next Memory Flower slightly to your right at the end of the path.

Upon leaving the Survivors Courtyard Bell head left and go down the stairs. You'll see the next Memory Flower on a small wooden workbench next to a giant hole

Memory Flower 13 is found at the Temple of Blue Fireflies Bell, which isn't accessible until players have reached the Survivors Courtyard Bell and made their way down from the north side of the map. Inside the Shrine, you'll find the Memory Flower on the altar.

Leave the Temple of Blue Fireflies and make your way back toward the Well of the Three Puppets in the center of the village. You'll come across a stone bridge that connects the two locations. On the right-hand side of the bridge, you'll find the next Memory Flower down below in the river.

Once you drop down the Well of The Three Puppets after successfully clearing out the threads, you'll find the next Memory Flower as soon as you load back in.

Those are all of the Memory Flowers for the Village of Lu. As you're going through the area, be sure to check out our main walkthrough so you don't miss a beat while exploring the map.

This page is still being worked on; check back soon for more information

Up Next: Village of Lu Memory Flower Locations

articles.title: Frank Miller Teases Sin City Future and Finally Drawing Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
articles.summary: IGN chatted with comic book icon Frank Miller about the long-awaited next Sin City graphic novel and the appeal of finally drawing the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles after 40 years.
articles.body:
Frank Miller is in one of the most prolific periods of his long comics career right now. The creator of iconic stories like The Dark Knight Returns and 300 is spinning up new projects and revisiting classic franchises, all while maintaining his own publishing company, Frank Miller Presents.

We were lucky enough to attend a roundtable interview at the Lucca Comics & Games Festival in Italy, where Miller reflected on his career and the current state of the industry, while also giving some updates on upcoming projects like Sin City: Blood & Dust and Invasive Species. Read on to see the highlights from that fascinating conversation.

Miller released a number of Sin City comics in the '90s and early '00s. But even with the Sin City movies drawing wider attention to the franchise, it's been quite some time since Miller has told any new stories in this seedy, noir-infused universe.

That's finally going to change soon. Miller has spent the past several years working on a new book first announced as Sin City 1858 and now called Sin City: Blood & Dust. As the title suggests, Blood & Dust is a prequel set in the Wild West era and detailing the original founding of Basin City. It's a massive undertaking for Miller, as unlike many of his current projects, he's writing and drawing the entire thing himself. But it's one that seems to be coming along nicely.

"I'm not sure exactly when the release date is planned for right now, but the project is very well along," Miller said. "I mean, I'm most of the way through it, and it's certainly all planned and plotted very carefully. And I've drawn, I'd say, about two-thirds of it. And so everything else should flow pretty quickly."

When asked how he's feeling about the project so far, Miller said, "Very good. Very good. It's certainly a departure. If you're going to take a break from a series for a long time, you might as well come back with a very different one."

Sin City: Blood & Dust is just one of several projects Miller is currently developing. He was asked if there were any particular books in the works he was especially excited to show to readers. Miller singled out Invasive Species, a new Dark Horse Comcis project that was announced at SDCC 2026 this past summer.

Invasive Species is a sci-fi comic that pairs Miller with artist Ryan Benjamin and colorist Alex Sinclair. Details about the book's plot were scarce before now, but Miller shed more light on it during the panel, revealing it to be a microscopic invasion story inspired by the COVID-19 pandemic.

"Invasive Species is what I'm particularly charged up about," Miller said. "It's a project I conceived during the height of the COVID pandemic where everyone was afraid to sneeze within a hundred yards of anybody else because everybody was so afraid and everyone was wearing masks. I think people were showering their masks. It was so paranoid. But what it reminded me of was those wonderful 1950s alien movies like Invasion of the Body Snatchers and Invaders From Mars and so on. They were all fear of a Russian invasion."

Miller continued, "But I thought we had biological warfare talk everywhere every which way now we've got viruses that we're all afraid of and as guys all locked inside not talking to each other. And I thought what perfect metaphor for our times. And so I made up a story where we were being invaded not by a bunch of spaceships, but by a virus, by little aliens that got inside, came in our ears."

One of the more interesting developments in the comic book world this year came when Miller was among numerous artists tapped to draw a cover for Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300. Miller is famously credited as a huge source of inspiration behind Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird's original TMNT comics, so it was a fun case of life imitating art.

We asked Miller for his thoughts on finally contributing to the TMNT franchise in an official capacity. He revealed that IDW didn't exactly have to twist his arm to get him on board.

"There's no agenda to all this stuff," Miller said. "They were kids when they were doing it in their clunky black-and-white comic. No one dreamed they would turn out to have this amazing property, which I think one of the main things they had was one of the best titles in history. So when they asked, I said, 'Sure.' I mean, they were big fans of mine and I thought that this will be fun. And then I sat down and said, 'What do I do with these guys?' I said, 'Well, look, stack them up.' I did it and they were real happy."

As for which Turtle is Miller's favorite, the artist replied, "Well, I have a favorite Renaissance painter. I say Michelangelo because the Sistine Ceiling is one of the best comic book pages I've ever seen."

Miller was able to make the leap from creating comics to directing films thanks to 2005's Sin City. Miller directed a segment of the film in collaboration with Robert Rodriguez and later did the same for the 2014 sequel. The Sin City movie paved the way for Miller to fully direct 2008's The Spirit, based on the classic Will Eisner hero.

The Spirit wasn't exactly well-received, critically or commercially, but it certainly brought a unique visual flourish to the property. We asked Miller if he had any desire to return behind the camera and direct another film at some point.

"Sure. Yeah. I mean, come on," Miller said. "It's an amazing field. It's an amazing form and it's like nothing else in the world."

Miller added, "I mean, that's like asking a kid if he wants to fly the Millennium Falcon."

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero, and he appears during the Against the Flow main quest. He's the first story boss
articles.body:
Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero , and he appears during the Against the Flow main quest. He's the first story boss you encounter in Weeping Creek Valley. Here are a few tips and strategies for how to beat him.

How to Defeat Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute

Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Blade , is a chaotic enemy who moves a bit erratically. You can wait a bit to see what he does to the other opponents nearby, but it’ll be your turn to fight soon. Here are all the special attacks you need to look out for:

The dying Iron Mask warned you about a rusty blade that makes you bleed, and he was talking about Frenzied Brute’s sword, Jagged Steel . Every one of his hits causes Bleed buildup, which drains your health. Do your best to avoid taking hits, either by parrying, dodging, or simply creating distance.

Use your new Sanguine Twin blades to extend your Sha-Chi combos by swapping weapons when your Sha-Chi runs low. You can also swap weapons defensively to refill your Sha-Chi meter before a guard break, allowing you to block more attacks. But watch for when the boss’s Sha-Chi meter refills – he’ll instantly start attacking again, ignoring and interrupting your combo.

Be ready to switch from offense to defense instantly whenever the Frenzied Brute recovers from being guard-broken. He also starts using longer combos under 50% HP, so try to be more patient as the battle goes on.

You obtain the Jagged Steel Main Weaponafter winning the fight. It’s a solid early-game status-effect weapon that inflicts Bleed on enemies as you land hits. At this point, you can replace either Sanguine or Sanguine Twin to equip it.
